name: POST /api/sla/clocks/:clock_id/cancel - End a promise that no longer applies
skipReason: DESTRUCTIVE TO THE SHARED CHAIN. Cancel ends the clock's life, and the create->capture chain in this suite yields exactly one clock_id which the satisfy path needs ALIVE. An automated case here would either consume that clock and break the satisfy definition downstream, or point at a fabricated id and fail as a 404 while proving nothing about cancellation. Covered by packages/sdk-sla/tests/clock.integration.test.ts, which creates a dedicated clock to cancel. This is a SHARED-PRODUCER lifecycle conflict, not a missing payload or an uncaptured path param - it is not the case MUST-49 forbids marking manual.
description: Cancel a clock with a mandatory reason — the subject withdrew, the request was a duplicate, the promise no longer applies. Any non-terminal clock can be cancelled (running, paused or breached); a satisfied or already-cancelled one returns 409 INVALID_CLOCK_TRANSITION. Returns 200. MANUAL: cancel ends the clock's life, and the create->capture chain in this suite yields exactly one clock_id which the satisfy path needs alive, so an automated case here would either destroy that chain or point at a fabricated id and fail as a 404 while proving nothing. Covered by packages/sdk-sla/tests/clock.integration.test.ts. Required: tenant_id, reason.

statusTransitions.note: at_risk is a DERIVED view over running/paused clocks approaching due_at (GET /api/sla/at-risk), not a stored state — the column can only hold the five values in fieldEnums.state.

transitions.note: a missed promise can still be kept, late — satisfied_at then sits after due_at so attainment still counts it as a miss

errorCases.when: a required field is missing from the request
the clock is already satisfied or cancelled
no valid tenant Bearer token on the request
